Organisms that feed on dead matter and convert it into nutrients are called: (a) Producers (b) Detritivores (c) Carnivores (d) Decomposers.
The accumulation of non-biodegradable matter or chemicals in living organisms is known as: (a) Ecological balance (b) Bioaccumulation (c) Carrying capacity (d) Biomagnification.
The amount of radiant energy stored at the producer level by photosynthesis is called: (a) Primary production (b) Homeostasis (c) Carrying capacity (d) All of the above.
The total number of living organisms at the various trophic levels of a food chain is depicted by: (a) Pyramid of numbers (b) Pyramid of energy (c) Pyramid of mass (d) All of these.
Which of the following is unidirectional in an ecosystem? (a) Flow of energy (b) Flow of nutrients (c) Flow of matter (d) All of these.
Which of the following are non-renewable energy sources? (a) Coal (b) Petroleum (c) Natural gas (d) All of these.
Solar energy can be harnessed using the principle of: (a) Photoelectric effect (b) Photo-oxidation (c) Photo-reduction (d) None of these.
Identify the environmental damage caused by mining: (a) Devegetation (b) Ground subsidence (c) Air and water pollution (d) All of these.
Variation among individuals of the same species is which type of biodiversity? (a) Genetic (b) Species (c) Ecosystem (d) Both (b) and (c).
The direct-use values of biodiversity include: (a) Food (b) Fuels (c) Medicines (d) All of these.
